archetype.name: Point Guard (with intermediate bite)
archetype.definition: A tenth-year Mahomes who now wins by getting the ball out on time to Kelce and his backs, avoiding sacks, and picking his spots in the 10-19 yard window rather than living off-script.

report.headline: A shorter, cleaner Mahomes: fewer sacks, sharper middle game, and a hot November.
report.take:
This is not the 2018 version and it isn't trying to be. Mahomes' intended air yards sit at 6.1 and his aggressiveness has dropped to 8.05% from 13.3% a year ago. He is throwing short of the sticks on average (-2.45), and his rushing has fallen off sharply, down 19 yards a game from last season. What he has traded for it is control. His sack rate of 3.9% ranks 5th, his pressure-to-sack rate of 18% ranks 6th, and his bad-throw rate of 11.7% ranks 5th. Completion percentage is up 4.1 points and yards per attempt up 0.86 on last year. The result is 0.155 EPA per dropback, 12th in the league and well clear of a league average below zero. That is very good, not dominant.

The engine is the intermediate game. His 43 throws between 10 and 19 air yards have produced 0.644 EPA apiece with a CPOE of 11.8. In total that is 27.7 EPA, more than his 137 short attempts added. Kelce is the main beneficiary at 0.448 EPA per target. Rookie-type back Emmett Johnson has been even better on a smaller sample, at 0.74 per target on 23 looks. Reid is also getting a lot out of Mahomes under center. Those dropbacks run at 0.24 EPA and a 58% success rate, against 0.124 from shotgun, which points to play-action and the run game, ranked 2nd by EPA, doing real work for him. The team still passes more than situations predict (4.6 over expected, 2nd), so the volume is there.

Two things in the numbers flatter or hide him. First, the red zone: 15 of his 19 touchdowns came there, on 48 attempts with a CPOE of 16.8. That touchdown rate (6.4%, 8th) is likely to cool even if the offense stays good. Second, the deep ball is broken. He is 29.4% on 20+ yard throws with a -8 CPOE, 2 interceptions and a 29.4% success rate. Xavier Worthy has drawn 50 targets for negative EPA, so a full co-lead target share is producing nothing. Third down hasn't been sharp either: a 34.6% conversion rate, with 5 of his 12 sacks coming on that down.

The recent run is real but needs context. Over the last three games he has thrown 10 touchdowns with no interceptions at 0.254 EPA per dropback, about 0.1 better than his season mark. That comes right after a flat two-week stretch: no touchdowns against the Chargers, then -5.2 EPA in Seattle. Across five games he's right on his season average. The baseline is a top-12, borderline top-8 efficient passer with low turnover and sack risk, plus occasional weeks like Atlanta when he opens the deep game back up.

strengths.title: The 10-19 yard window
strengths.body: Intermediate throws are where his season is made: 0.644 EPA per attempt and an 11.8 CPOE on 43 throws, the biggest single source of his passing value. It fits a design built on timing routes and play-action, with Kelce working the middle. Forty-odd attempts is a moderate sample, so expect some cooling, but accuracy at this depth has been a career constant rather than a fluke.

strengths.title: Sacks back to his old norm
strengths.body: His pressure-to-sack rate had ballooned to 27-29% in 2024-25. It is back down to 18%, in line with what he posted from 2019 through 2023, and his overall sack rate ranks 5th. The quicker, shorter decision tree is the cause: fewer held balls, fewer bad throws (11.7%, 5th). Because it rests on design and how fast he decides rather than luck, it should hold, though a banged-up line will test it.

strengths.title: Under center and the backs
strengths.body: Under-center dropbacks run at 0.24 EPA with a 58% success rate, roughly double his shotgun efficiency. The backs give him easy yards: Emmett Johnson is at 0.74 EPA per target on 23 looks. With the run game ranked 2nd by EPA, defenses have to respect the fake, and that is a structural edge, not a hot streak.

concerns.title: Deep ball has gone missing
concerns.body: On 20+ yard throws he is completing 29.4% with a -8 CPOE and 2 of his 4 interceptions. A deep-threat completion rate is always low, but a negative CPOE says these are misses, not just low-percentage shots. Worthy's 50 targets producing negative total EPA is the same problem from the receiving side. The lower aggressiveness looks partly like a response to this, and until it changes, his ceiling depends on Atlanta-style weeks rather than his weekly floor.

concerns.title: Red-zone TD rate will cool
concerns.body: Fifteen of his 19 touchdowns came inside the 20, on 48 attempts with a 16.8 CPOE. That red-zone accuracy is far above anything else in his profile. The offense will keep getting there, but expect the touchdown share to soften, which matters more for fantasy than for his real efficiency.

concerns.title: Third downs and a thinning line
concerns.body: Third down is the weak spot: a 34.6% conversion rate at an average of 7 yards to go, with 5 sacks. The line already allows hits at a middling rate (21st). Tackle Jaylon Moore (87% of snaps) is now out and guard Trey Smith (91%) is in concussion protocol. Long-yardage downs are where the quick-game approach is most exposed if the protection slips.

trend.note: A two-week lull against the Chargers and Seattle (0 TD, then -5.2 EPA) gave way to three strong games: 10 TDs, 0 INTs, and 0.254 EPA per dropback, about 0.1 above his season rate. Two of those came against middling-to-weak defenses, so it's a real upswing, but not quite a new level.

nextGame.headline: Worst pass defense in the league; the spread is the only cap.
nextGame.body:
Arizona's pass defense is last in EPA allowed (0.266 per play) and near the bottom in both deep (29th) and short (28th) EPA. It allows the 31st-most touchdowns per game to quarterbacks. Its pass rush is middling (sack rate 14th), so the clean-pocket, get-it-out approach should work, and tight ends have beaten their usual output against it (TE1 +2.9 PPR over average, 29th). Starting safety Andrew Wingard (86% of snaps) is out for an extended stretch. That thins the back end exactly where Mahomes wins in the 10-19 window and could invite a few more deep shots. The catch is script. Kansas City is a 16.5-point favorite against an offense now without Gardner Minshew for the season, and with a 41.5 total, a comfortable second-half lead could hand the game to the 2nd-ranked run game. He has stayed efficient when leading by 9+ (0.206 EPA), but volume is the risk, not efficiency.

On his side, Moore is out at tackle and Smith is questionable after a concussion. Losing both interior and edge starters would test the quick-game protection, especially on third down. Kenneth Walker is out, which points more backfield targets toward Emmett Johnson, whose per-target efficiency has been the best on the team. The site lists Mahomes himself as questionable, but his last practice report was full participation and he played 95% of snaps in Atlanta, so nothing in the dossier suggests his availability is in doubt.

keyMatchups.title: Middle of the field vs thin secondary
keyMatchups.body: Arizona ranks 32nd in pass EPA allowed and is now without Wingard for an extended period. Mahomes' best zone, 10-19 yards, is exactly what a short-handed safety group struggles to cover. Expect Kelce to work the seams.

keyMatchups.title: Blowout script vs passing volume
keyMatchups.body: A 16.5-point spread against a backup-quarterback offense points to a big lead. With Kansas City's run game ranked 2nd, the second half could be mostly handoffs. His efficiency when ahead is fine; the question is how many dropbacks he gets.

keyMatchups.title: Patched line on third down
keyMatchups.body: With Moore out and Smith questionable, his protection gets weaker on the down where he is already least effective. Arizona's sack rate is only mid-pack, which helps.

nextGame.watch: Whether he keeps the Atlanta-style aggressiveness and takes intermediate and deep shots at a safety-depleted secondary early, before the score turns it into a run-game afternoon.

restOfSeason.body:
The foundation holds: sack avoidance back to his career norm, low bad-throw and interception rates, a strong intermediate game, and an offense that still passes more than situations require. Expect him to settle around 255-285 passing yards a game with efficiency in the top 8-12 range, and few turnovers. His interception rate is well below last year's and fits a shorter, quicker game.

What regresses is touchdown efficiency. His red-zone accuracy and a 6.4% TD rate are running hot, so plan on about two scores a game rather than the three-plus of the last three weeks. Rushing has become a minor factor. The upside lever is the deep ball: if he and Worthy start connecting, the ceiling rises; if not, his weekly range stays narrower than his name suggests. Offensive-line health over the next few weeks is the main downside risk.
swingFactors: Return of Moore and Smith up front
Whether the deep game with Worthy comes alive

confidence.note: Nine starts with a clear style change that fits his pre-2024 profile, but red-zone luck and line injuries add noise.
